policy:
policy BakeryPolicy {
  allow read CakeOrders(customer, email, pickup, status, address)
  allow contact CakeOrders.email
  deny reveal CakeOrders.address
  limit sends 200 per day
  send only between 09:00 and 21:00
  approval batch valid 1 hour max 10 preview 5
}
sheets: sheet CakeOrders "CakeOrders" { customer: Text, email: Email, pickup: Date, status: Text, price: Money, address: Text private }
program:
procedure BakeryWinBack {
  about "Nudge customers whose pickup date was long ago"
  policy BakeryPolicy
  sheet CakeOrders "CakeOrders" { customer: Text, email: Email, pickup: Date, status: Text, price: Money, address: Text private }
  trigger every monday at 18:00

  let all = fetch CakeOrders
  let old = filter all where days_between(pickup, today()) >= 30 and status != "cancelled"
  let oldest = sort old by pickup first 10
  let msgs = draft each r in oldest up to 10 email to r.email subject "We miss you": "Hi {r.customer default 'there'}, it's been a while! We'd love to see you again at the bakery."
  let ok = request batch approval of msgs from owner timeout 2 hours else stop "batch not approved"
  send ok
}
sop:
Please set up the automation to nudge customers whose pickup date was more than 30 days ago. It should run every Monday at 6:00 PM and send no more than 10 messages each time. Only the top 10 oldest orders should be considered for this nudge. Each message should be sent to the customer's email with the subject "We miss you" and the body "Hi {customer name}, it's been a while! We'd love to see you again at the bakery."

The batch of messages must be approved within 2 hours or the process will stop. Do not request further approvals after that. The automation should not send any messages outside the hours of 9:00 AM to 9:00 PM daily and should not exceed 200 messages per day.

Thank you!

policy ClinicPolicy {
  allow read Visits(patient, phone, status)
  allow write Visits(status)
  allow contact Visits.phone
  deny reveal Visits.diagnosis
  limit sends 150 per day
  send only between 07:30 and 19:00
}
sheets: sheet Visits "Visits" { patient: Text, phone: Phone, starts: DateTime, status: Text, copay: Money, diagnosis: Text private }
program:
procedure ClinicFollowUpAfterWait {
  about "Contact a new patient, then follow up once"
  policy ClinicPolicy
  sheet Visits "Visits" { patient: Text, phone: Phone, starts: DateTime, status: Text, copay: Money, diagnosis: Text private }
  trigger when new row r in Visits

  let first = draft sms to r.phone: "Hi {r.patient default 'there'}, thanks for choosing the clinic! Reply with any questions."
  let ok1 = request approval of first from owner timeout 1 day else stop "first message not approved"
  send ok1
  update r set status = "contacted"
  wait 3 days
  let all = fetch Visits
  let now_r = find all where phone == r.phone else stop "row was removed"
  if now_r.status == "done" or now_r.status == "cancelled" {
    stop "already handled"
  }
  let second = draft sms to now_r.phone: "Hi {now_r.patient default 'there'}, just checking in. Is there anything we can help with?"
  let ok2 = request approval of second from owner timeout 1 day else stop "follow-up not approved"
  send ok2
}
sop:
Please set up an automation that contacts new patients after their visit and follows up three days later if they haven't been contacted yet. The messages should be sent via SMS. Here are the details:

- The first message should say: "Hi [Patient Name], thanks for choosing the clinic! Reply with any questions."
- The follow-up message should say: "Hi [Patient Name], just checking in. Is there anything we can help with?"

Conditions:
- Only send these messages between 7:30 AM and 7:00 PM.
- Send no more than 150 messages per day.
- Only send to new patients (status = "contacted").
- Do not include medical diagnosis in either message.

Only the clinic owner should approve the messages before they are sent. Stop if the owner does not approve within one day.
